title: A GIF or HEIC export on a busy Mac never loses a frame or comes out empty
goal: When the Mac is under heavy load, an exported GIF can silently come out a frame short, and a HEIC can come out with no pictures at all, with no error. A person exporting should always get every frame, or be told the export failed.
notes: CI red on main, seen on run 45583153492 (commit 34bcb4395, Test slice 2 of 3, 2026-11-25). Command: gh run view 45583153492 --log-failed | grep -A2 'recorded an issue'. Output: 'short gif at high held (count: 48, width: 640, height: 400) and then (count: 47, width: 640, height: 400) pictures'; 'longer heic at small held (count: 40, width: 480, height: 300) and then (count: 0, width: 0, height: 0) pictures'; 'longer gif at high held (count: 95, ...) and then (count: 96, ...)'; GIF bytes 113275 then 111114 and 205656 then 208277. The test took 648 s and the slice 955 s, so that runner was starved. Not reproduced on this Mac. Likely place, from reading only: Sources/PhotonzMedia/VideoExporter.swift exportAnimated, 'guard var frame = try? await generator.image(at: time).image else { continue }' skips a frame whose read threw. The HEIC with 0 pictures is not explained: CGImageDestinationFinalize returned true. Found by the runner of an-edit-with-50-tracks-and-100-clips-scrolls-pla.
acceptance: A frame that cannot be read is read again before it is given up on, and a frame given up on for good is an error or is logged, never a silent gap: a test makes the first read of a frame fail and the written GIF still holds every frame
An animated file that finishes with no readable pictures is an error, never a success: a test covers it
The test 'written twice, a GIF is the same file and a HEIC the same pictures' passes on CI, and its expectations are unchanged

log.note: Triage 2026-11-25: ran the command in the notes. It shows what they say: gif 48 then 47 and 95 then 96 frames, heic 40 then 0 pictures, sizes 113275/111114 and 205656/208277. The next full CI run (45608791712) was green, so it is a busy-machine fault. The skip is there to read in exportAnimated (a frame whose read throws is passed over and its time given to the next). Not reproduced on this Mac. Stays p1: a lost frame with no error is lost work.
